This game is like if you took Sekiro, Ghost of Tsushima, and Onimusha and made it chinese - and thats exactly what youll get here. Its linear, it backtracks, it has souls, secrets, a variety of weapons, and the dodge/deflect/parry system isn't anywhere near as easy as i had expected before playing. If you love Sekiro combat then this is exactly what youll get here, if you like the cinematic combat of Onimusha, and if you like the executions of Ghost of Tsushima then that too is what youll absolutely get with this game as well.

What surprised me most, however, is that they took the time to add a whole anime series of the story into the game. No, im not kidding, and its actually animated very well. Combined with the graphics, the flow of combat, the secrets, the missions, and the whole extra stuff that mind you they didnt even need to add like the anime series ... this game is definitely a strong recommendation from me!

Although, is it better than Sekiro, Ghost of Tsushima, or Onimusha? Pretty subjective. To me the story is quite bland and confusing, the color pallet of the overall scenes are a bit washed out and favors a more grey and black approach which isnt pleasant to the eyes. Despite those negatives i still think this game is quite good and innovates the soulslike genre to the next level.

If you're like me—someone who doesn't care much about the story, but just wants insanely satisfying and badass combat—what kind of crazy-ass game is this? It’s got that Hack-and-Slash flow mixed with Soulslike mechanics, and it is fucking epic. Plus, the optimization is top-notch, and the visuals are drop-dead gorgeous. For me, it's a solid 10/10. The combat has been fantastic so far. It's incredibly fluid, responsive, and genuinely fun to play.

Performance has also been great on my system. I'm getting anywhere between 60–120 FPS at 1440p, with all graphics settings maxed out, path tracing enabled, DLSS Quality, and frame generation disabled.

So far, I'm very impressed with both the gameplay and the optimisation. Can't wait to put more hours into this game!

Quick tip for performance, make sure you download the day 1 patch and if you are using an Nvida card use the Nvida driver 617.42.

Phantom Blade Zero It's EXACTLY what the trailers promised.

I genuinely don't understand all the "assisted combat" and "handholding" complaints. I've played pretty much every FromSoftware game, including NG+ runs on several of them, so I'm no stranger to getting my ass kicked. And trust me, Hardcore difficulty has been doing a fine job of reminding me of that.

But what really sells this game is the swordplay.

The combat feels fresh. Sure, some mechanics are familiar, but it feels like the developers are trying to create something of their own rather than copy-pasting an existing formula.

Enemies block, parry, and counterattack. Clashing swords with two or three enemies, going toe-to-toe until someone finally lands that perfect parry, feels absolutely GLORIOUS. It's like playing through a choreographed martial arts movie, except nobody told the enemies they're supposed to lose.

So far, I've discovered weapon customization, some awesome boss encounters, and mechanics that keep surprising me. I've heard later bosses get even crazier, but the Axe Master already gave me a free lesson in humility. Had to actually learn the mechanics before coming back to return the favor.

Gorgeous visuals, satisfying combat, and exactly the cinematic sword fights we were promised.

10/10 sword clashes. My orange meter would disagree.

This is the best Soulslike game I’ve ever played. Some aspects are different from traditional Souls games—for example, you don’t lose your souls when you die. But the game is incredibly well-optimized, with great FPS performance and absolutely incredible combat, unlike anything I’ve experienced in any other game.

One of the most interesting things is that every weapon has its own unique playstyle, making each one feel different. The world-building and atmosphere are also amazing.

Another great feature is that you can refund all the upgrades from your weapons and transfer them to another weapon, so you don’t have to spend hours farming resources.

Huge thanks to the development team for creating such an amazing game. I really hope to see more games like this in the future!

After playing the first 1.5 hours, I can confidently say that Phantom Blade Zero by S-Game is absolute perfection.

Here are my quick thoughts from the first chapter:

Flawless Optimization & Smooth Combat: The performance is ridiculously smooth. Every movement, strike, and dodge feels tight, responsive, and beautifully animated.

Skill-Based Parry System: Unlike Sekiro, this isn't just about L1/LB button spamming. The parry mechanics require actual timing and deliberate inputs, making every counter-attack incredibly satisfying.

Not a Pure Souls-like: It borrows great elements from the genre, but it carves its own path. For example, enemies do not respawn when you rest, keeping the pacing tight and rewarding.

S-Game delivered something truly special here. If you love fast-paced wuxia action and crisp combat systems, do not hesitate. Absolutely recommended!

Bottom Line: This game is already a strong GOTY contestant of 2026. Absolute perfection. S-Game delivered!
